importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — a luxury AC van, a cluster of FRP portable cabins, and a bio-toilet unit are visually unrecognisable as the same category. Buyers use the image to identify the unit type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.
Rental rates are compared aggressively across vendors once unit type matches. Indian B2B buyers shortlist on per-day or per-month rate; price is a primary decision lever at the listing tile stage.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Long-term construction/project deployments are quoted per month; large multi-unit event deployments use per unit per day. Unit must always be shown alongside price — a per-day rate vs a per-event rate for a 3-day wedding creates real price comparison confusion.
importance_ranking.reason: Per day, per month, and per event are all active in this market. Price cannot be compared or interpreted without the billing unit shown explicitly.

Buyers arrive knowing their broad requirement (van vs cabin, approximate capacity). Specs such as cabin type, seat configuration, and waste handling confirm fit after initial price and image shortlisting — they are qualifiers, not discovery signals.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No nationally recognised brand with buyer recall exists in this category; the market is fragmented across regional operators and buyers search by location, unit type, and price rather than operator name.
importance_ranking.reason: Service reliability, geographic coverage, and operator track record are evaluated during vendor selection — particularly for large municipal or construction contracts — but only after unit type, capacity, and price are confirmed.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the unit IS — VIP/AC cabin vs standard multi-seater vs urinal cabin are non-interchangeable and carry a 5–10x price differential across the range.
Indian vs Western vs Combi seat configuration is non-interchangeable for the buyer's use case and drives a meaningful price delta between standard and Western/Combi-configured units.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Event and construction buyers specify exact seat count (4, 6, or 10 seats) as a primary procurement requirement; sellers need this to confirm fleet availability and quote accurately.

AC luxury variants command a significantly higher rental rate and serve a distinct buyer segment (weddings, VIP events, corporate functions); sellers need this to match their fleet offering to the buyer's requirement.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Seat count directly determines which units a seller can supply — a seller with only 4-seater vans cannot fulfil a 10-seater requirement, making this the primary fleet-matching signal.

Physical form of the unit (vehicle-mounted van vs individual portable cabin vs trolley) determines fleet type compatibility and site logistics — sellers need this to confirm they have the right equipment.

missing_important_specs.why_important: A seller with a small fleet cannot fulfil a 50-unit municipal event deployment; quantity is the primary fulfilment-capacity signal that determines whether a seller can respond at all.
Per-day event rental and per-month construction site deployment require different logistics, pricing structures, and service schedules — sellers need this to quote accurately.

Row of three standalone portable toilet cabins in white and blue FRP, individual box units placed side by side on open ground at an outdoor event site, natural daylight, front-facing view, no branding or text.
